what: Crawls content that may be used to train OpenAI's generative AI foundation models. Disallowing it signals content should not be used for training.

Surfaces websites in ChatGPT search results. Sites opted out are not shown in ChatGPT search answers, though they can still appear as navigational links. OpenAI says robots.txt changes take about 24 hours to apply.
Visits pages for user actions in ChatGPT and Custom GPTs. Not used for automatic crawling. OpenAI says that because these actions are user-initiated, robots.txt rules may not apply.
Validates the safety of landing pages submitted as ads on ChatGPT. Only visits pages submitted as ads; data is not used to train foundation models.
Collects web content that could contribute to training Anthropic's models. Restricting it signals the site's future materials should be excluded from training datasets.
Indexes content to improve Claude search results. Disabling it may reduce visibility in Claude search results.
Fetches pages when people ask Claude questions. Anthropic says its bots honor robots.txt; disabling Claude-User prevents retrieval in response to user queries.
Surfaces and links websites in Perplexity search results. Perplexity says it is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models. Changes may take up to 24 hours.
Visits pages to answer user questions in Perplexity. Perplexity says that because a user requested the fetch, it generally ignores robots.txt rules.

Standalone control token, no separate crawler. Manages whether content Google crawls may be used to train future Gemini models and for grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. Does not affect Google Search inclusion or ranking.
Google Search crawler (including Discover, Images, Video mode, News). Blocking it removes pages from Google Search crawling.
Generic Google crawler used by product teams, for example one-off crawls for internal research and development. Does not affect a specific product.
Crawls requested by site owners for building Vertex AI Agents. No effect on Google Search. Also matches Googlebot rules.

Powers search in Spotlight, Siri and Safari. Apple says crawled data may also be used to help train Apple foundation models. If robots.txt does not mention Applebot but mentions Googlebot, Applebot follows the Googlebot rules.
Does not crawl. Disallowing it opts content out of training Apple's foundation models; pages can still appear in Apple search results.
Builds Common Crawl's open repository of web crawl data, freely available to anyone. Common Crawl documents a robots.txt block and notes some crawlers falsely identify as CCBot.
Crawls for use cases such as training foundation AI models or improving products by indexing content directly.
Improves Meta AI search results; allowing it helps Meta cite and link content in Meta AI responses.
Fetches individual links at a user's request, including agentic AI tasks. Meta says it may bypass robots.txt.
Builds link previews (title, description, image) when links are shared on Facebook, Instagram or Messenger. May bypass robots.txt for security or integrity checks.
